overview.definition: An automation spec is a structured rule system that defines how content is classified, structured, and organized when building and scaling a website.
overview.purpose: To formalize decision-making so content creation becomes consistent, repeatable, and eventually automatable.
overview.scope: It governs how queries, topics, and entities map to pages, hubs, and site structure.

decision_rules: Defines how content is classified into hub, pillar, or section types
Defines how queries map to page types
Defines how topics are grouped into clusters
structure_rules: Defines required sections inside each page type
Ensures consistency across generated or created pages
routing_rules: Defines where content lives in the site hierarchy
linking_rules: Defines internal linking between hubs and pillar pages
Ensures hubs link down and pillars link up
deduplication_rules: Prevents multiple pages targeting the same intent
Ensures one entity equals one canonical page

runtime_behavior: Does not automatically build or deploy a website
Does not modify a site without an execution system
Does not function as runtime application code
does_not_do.note: Becomes active only when implemented in a content generation or routing pipeline

data_layer.description: Raw inputs used for decision making

spec_layer.description: Rule system that interprets and structures data
spec_layer.example: book vs movie queries → pillar page

execution_layer.description: System or human process that applies rules
execution_layer.function: Generates or organizes content based on spec rules

website_layer.description: Final rendered pages seen by users

classification.example: IF query contains 'book vs movie' THEN type = PILLAR

routing.description: Assigns content to URLs or hubs

seo_strategy: Structure matters more than volume at early stage
site_model: Section = sub-intent within a pillar page
